answers.answer: Consider refactoring these nested conditionals to use early returns (guard clauses). Handing invalid/edge cases first keeps the main logic linear, easier to read, and simpler to test.

Think of Service B like a busy kitchen counter. If Service A makes direct calls, it has to stand at the counter waiting for its food while blocking all other work. By using a message queue—like a ticket hook—Service A leaves its order and immediately returns to helping users, while Service B processes orders at a steady pace without crashing during peak lunch rushes.
